memory_candidates.content: When porting a source engine's sequential two-if-block gate (verify-or-redispatch, then act-on-success) into a consolidated engine that must ALSO preserve unconditional prior behavior for a disabled mode, combine the mode flag into both conditions rather than nesting: gate 1 becomes `if [ mode=true ] && [ state=false ]; then ...`, and gate 2 (wrapping everything downstream that must not run on re-dispatch) becomes `if [ mode!=true ] || [ state=true ]; then ... fi`. The second condition's OR short-circuits in the disabled mode, so the state variable is never actually read there, preserving the guarantee that it's 'only ever read inside the mode guard' even though the wrapping if itself isn't nested inside a separate mode check.

When a plan requires 'the patterns/text as they landed in the file, not re-derived from the plan', extract them from the file with `grep -oP` (or equivalent) into shell variables and re-run the same fixture matrix against those extracted values, rather than re-typing the pattern from the plan text. This catches transcription errors (a missed backslash, a copy-paste of the WRONG source engine's version) that a purely visual diff review would miss.
